content:
Survey complete. I documented all 5 health timing tests in `src/health/mod.rs`:

1. **heartbeat_updates_with_shared_state** (line 1460) - 1500ms sleep - validates shared state updates propagate to heartbeat
2. **atomic_write_never_produces_partial** (line 1623) - 100ms × 10 iterations - validates atomic write-rename never produces partial JSON
3. **heartbeat_files_dont_collide_across_adapter_pools** (line 1846) - 1500ms sleep - validates distinct files for same worker name across adapters
4. **heartbeat_uses_cross_workspace_bead_workspace** (line 1918) - 1500ms sleep - validates cross-workspace bead reporting
5. **worker_liveness_detection_integration** (line 4654) - 2s sleep - validates liveness across refresh cycles

All use `tokio::time::sleep` because the heartbeat emitter runs in a native `std::thread`, so real wall-clock time is required for the emitter to write updates.

Also noted `emitter_exits_after_consecutive_failures` (line 1730) which indirectly causes wall-clock waits via `emitter_loop`'s `std::thread::sleep`.

No code changes made - documentation only as requested.
